QUIC client flood test that sends signed messages on many streams and can reclaim packet metadata.

# Purpose
This file defines a QUIC client test program that connects to a remote peer, completes the handshake, and then sends a continuous flood of short application data streams. It uses `fd_quic` client APIs, a UDP socket wrapper, and a clock source to drive QUIC service processing and packet transmission. The program also supports an `--unreliable` mode that reclaims packet metadata as if packets were acknowledged, which lets the test exercise connection and stream handling under forced loss-like conditions.

The file also builds test payloads before sending them. It generates signed reference messages for every size from `1` byte to `1232 - 64 - 32` bytes, verifies each message with `fd_ed25519_verify`, and stores them in packet buffers used by `fd_quic_stream_send`. The [`main`](<#main>) function parses command-line options such as destination IP, destination port, gateway MAC, page size, page count, NUMA index, and batch size, then creates the workspace, QUIC client, and UDP socket before entering an endless retry loop that restarts the client after connection failure.
